abstract: In 1997, Alon and Kim proposed an asymptotic edge-coloring bound motivated by a bound on the number of edges in intersecting uniform hypergraphs. The Alon--Kim conjecture asserts that, for fixed integers $k\ge t\ge1$ and $\varepsilon>0$, every $k$-uniform multihypergraph $H$ in which any two distinct edges intersect in at most $t$ vertices satisfies $\chi'(H)\le(t-1+\frac{1}{t}+\varepsilon)\Delta(H)$ whenever $\Delta(H)$ is sufficiently large. In this paper, we prove the Alon--Kim conjecture. Our method combines finite-dimensional convex optimization with probabilistic methods.
hook: The 1997 Alon-Kim conjecture on edge-coloring hypergraphs is proved.
summary: The authors prove that hypergraphs whose edges pairwise share at most t vertices can be edge-colored with about (t-1+1/t) times the maximum degree colors, as Alon and Kim conjectured. The proof combines convex optimization with probabilistic methods. The bound is asymptotic, so it holds only once the maximum degree is sufficiently large, and it is a preprint not yet refereed.
title: The Proof of the Alon--Kim Conjecture
